response.consequence: Addresses listed in BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS, which the handler is meant to exclude, still get emails. Existing attendees get a duplicate notification. This can be used to send unwanted mail to arbitrary addresses.
response.explanation: The handler builds `uniqueGuests` by dropping existing attendees and blacklisted emails, and only those are saved. The notification call then uses `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered input. A blacklisted address, or an existing attendee, still receives an 'added to event' email even though it was not added. Duplicates inside the input are also emailed more than once.

other_findings.consequence: Team admins who are not owners are wrongly refused. Mixed-case blacklisted emails bypass the blacklist. Duplicate attendees can be created. A very large list causes unbounded work and mass emailing.
other_findings.explanation: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so it only passes for someone who is both. A team admin who is not an owner is denied unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. Separately, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`. Server-side uniqueness is only checked against existing attendees, not within the input. The blacklist comparison is case-sensitive against the raw guest string, while the blacklist entries are lowercased. A large list triggers one translation lookup per attendee, a createMany, a calendar update and emails. Any attendee, or anyone matching the email, can submit such a list.
other_findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles, and the guest list has no size bound or server-side dedupe
